messages:
harper (support): Hey team — customer report: after the March rollout their README output now has stray '#' characters inside headers and inline code.

anne (CS): can you paste the original prompt and the before/after responses?

harper (support): Customer prompt:
```
Write a short README section for installation.
Include a brief code sample.
```

harper (support): Pre-rollout response (from their audit log):
```
# Installation
Run `make install`
```

harper (support): Post-rollout response (what they get now):
```
###Installation
Run `###make install`
```

harper (support): They say this started immediately after canary -> prod on 2026-03-15 04:20 UTC.

anne (CS): :eyes: tagging eng. dan / kai can you take a look? This looks like extra hash tokens inserted during decoding or token boundary issues.

dan (infra): pulling worker logs for the rollout window.

dan (infra): sample worker log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T04:20:13Z] decode_step id=xyz emitted_token="#" prob=0.0021 source=kvcache
[2026-03-15T04:20:13Z] decode_step id=xyz emitted_token="#" prob=0.0019 source=kvcache
```

kai (ML Eng): We switched to quant-opt kernels in v2.1; prefix caching code paths were modified. Possible boundary doubling when a cached suffix overlaps a tokenization break. Can you paste the exact API payload (including stop sequences) the customer used?

harper (support): Here's the anonymized request they provided:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-v2.1-quant-opt",
  "input": "## Installation\nRun `make install`",
  "stop": ["\n#", "###"],
  "max_tokens": 60
}
```

kai (ML Eng): Interesting: they used stop sequences containing '#'. If prefix cache returned partial token boundaries, the model might emit the stop-char as separate tokens leading to duplication when concatenating cached prefix + new decoding output.

anne (CS): Customer impact = high (docs generation pipeline). CS ticket CS-4381. They've asked for rollback or hotfix.

dan (infra): We can pin their org to v2.0 immediately. Rollback requires approval but pinning is quick. Deploy-bot: can we rollback the global rollout?

deploy-bot: Canary r-20260315-02 completed -> rollout to 100% at 2026-03-15T04:20:12Z. Rollback requires manual action. Indicate approved.

kai (ML Eng): I'll reproduce with repro script: short sequences, inline backticks and stop sequences including '#'. Local run reproduces hashes injected when cache hits occur. Root cause appears to be token boundary handling in cached prefix reconstruction.

kai (ML Eng): Plan: patch prefix-reassembly to ensure byte-aligned token boundaries and add an extra check that stop sequences are not split across cache seam. Will test on canary, then push hotfix. ETA 3-4 hours.

harper (support): I've informed customer, offered workaround: pin to v2.0 or add a post-processing filter to strip runs of leading '#' in headers. They accepted pinning for now.

anne (CS): Good. Keep updates here. Once patch lands, please include token-diff logs and a small test matrix showing before/after for stop sequences and inline code.

kai (ML Eng): Will do. Posting initial patch link: <internal-git/patch/1212> once CI passes.

harper (support): Thanks — will mark CS ticket P1 and update customer when v2.1 patch deployed.
